newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates, spot end up.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates, spot end up.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mostly up on Wednesday, with institutions borrowing money to trade new domestic A share issues, traders said.
The annual rate for the most active seven-day contract rose to 11.96 percent from 10.00 percent on Tuesday.
Turnover rose to 6.42 million lots from 5.57 million. One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
Jiangsu Zongyi, an A share, made its debut on the Shanghai bourse today and Sichuan Pharmaceutical issued A shares, attracting much liquidity from the repo market, traders said.
Traders expect the repo rates to keep on rising in the next few days because of more new A share issues and listings.

Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mostly up on Wednesday after prices hit bottom on Tuesday but trading was dull, with most investors sidelined on weak market sentiment, traders said.
The most active 10-year bond that matures in June 2006, a market barometer, rose slightly to 120.15 yuan from 120.00.
Combined volume of the eight-contract market shrank to 658,579 lots from 773,433 lots.

"Bargain-hunting supported the 10-year bond today after it hit a bottom line at 120 yuan yesterday," said one trader. "Other investors are likely to follow up and buy tomorrow, with the price of the bond still very low."

But traders said market sentiment was poor after the contracts had been on a downward trend for weeks because of a demand for tighter liquidity with the approach of the year-end and a bull-run on the A share market.
China's first seven-year bond will make its debut on Thursday and traders expect it to perform poorly due to weak market conditions. -- Shanghai newsroom (86-21) 6279-7004
